float_conversion_routes.classification: finite input-bounded conversion; preserve predicate classification first
float_conversion_routes.reason: All three call paths supply len of real []interface{} input. After finite classification, floor first and reject outside [-length,length). Real interface-slice length is bounded below signed64 by its element storage; float rounding of length cannot reach 2^63. The final integer index range check rejects any rounded-edge discrepancy. NaN must take the legacy truthy branch before this helper, while infinity retains D1001 refusal. Exact311d misses NaN classification; native170 evidence demonstrates this gap, proposed evidence overlay corrects it. No blanket NaN-to-index-zero rule.

other_integer_and_index_routes.rule: Integer-only casts: nonnegative len/cap or checked length/product convert int to uint64; count arithmetic is checked before growth/reservation. uint(0)>>1 forms signed64 MaxInt. No float language value is accepted by these helpers. All four targets have the same integer widths. See all sites, including constants, in typed-conversions.json.

meter_json_number.go:23–43 widens signed int/int8/int16/int32 to int64 and unsigned counterparts to uint64. Existing int64/uint64 are unchanged. Float input uses AppendFloat and never integer conversion. Exact input/value-graph acceptance remains separately governed; these cases do not widen it.

Parser ParseInt(octets,16,32) checks the error before rune conversion; JSON hex decoder handles four checked hexadecimal digits so rune accumulation <=65535. Other byte/rune conversions widen checked code points or are fixed -1 sentinels. UTF8 range positions are native byte indices, not float values.

Compiler-owned regexp/syntax.Compile returns Start from a uint32 fragment index; Go1.26.7 syntax.Parse limits compiled size to128MiB/40=3355443 instructions before publication, below2^32. Two private uint32(program.Start) casts preserve that value. instruction.Arg flags are unsigned fixed-width casts; pc/capture bounds are checked before indexing. No caller-owned syntax.Prog is admitted. Full public compiler admission and physical proof remain owed.

other_integer_and_index_routes.route: Round decimal exponent parsing and arithmetic
other_integer_and_index_routes.rule: functions.go:2914/2942 Atoi reads only exponent suffix of fixed %g float64 formatting. Finite decimal exponent is within[-324,308]; NaN/Inf forms have no e suffix and retain zero exponent. After semantic precision conversion, exp+precision and exp-precision deliberately use defined signed64 wrap; they are formatted as decimal strings, not used as Go formatting precision or allocation sizes. ParseFloat handles any resulting huge exponent through its guarded parser.

ParseFloat is first and returns a float; failed parsing takes explicit-base ParseInt with bitSize64 at functions.go:2728/2732/2736 and returns only if err==nil. Range rejection is explicit before int64-to-float result conversion. It is not float-to-index/precision conversion and retains D3030 on invalid input. No saturation or new nonfinite policy applies.

Go1.26.7 public strconv delegates to internal/strconv. genericFtoa extracts float bits, then uses integer mantissa/exponent Dragonbox/fixed/decimal algorithms; no unbounded language float-to-int index conversion. exp/mantissa bit widths are11/52 (or8/23); fixed shortest/%g formats select bounded digits. ParseFloat exponent scan only accumulates while e<10000, then scans remaining bytes without growing e. ParseInt validates base/bitSize and overflow before casting; rounding temporary exponent strings can be signed64 values but are parsed as float exponents through that bounded scan. Numeric formatting work/physical cost is a separate pre-existing4043 obligation.

Retained abs/floor/ceil/round keep floating values; Round uses bit operations or architecture floating instructions, not language integer indices. Numeric arithmetic calls Mod; the selected four builds use generic mod, whose Frexp/Ldexp helpers extract/reassemble bounded integer exponent bits. No casts of an unbounded floating value to an index occur on these paths. Excluded datetime logarithm/power and formatNumber/formatBase rounding casts are separately listed.

reachability_closure.AST: meter_ast.go handles path/literals/variables/apply/partial/regex/transform/function/parent/name/unary/bind/block/condition/binary plus predicate/group stages; recursive paths enter the same dispatcher. Neither generic legacy evaluate nor range/date formatting is an escape. Parsing and regex compilation precede evaluation.
reachability_closure.callables: meter_builtin_value.go values1..19 resolve through meter_invoke.go. Aliases keep immutable identities; partial expansion, compositions, transforms and closed contains callbacks dispatch back through those private routes. Generic host Function/native callback/global frame is not an admitted input. Selected extension values cannot be captured or called indirectly.
reachability_closure.legacy_helpers: Shared19 bodies remain in functions.go, but private scope redirects recursive stringification, lookup, boolean/copy, regex and contains paths to private helpers. Scan covers all shared body closures, not just names starting with meter. The legacy matcher conversions above are deliberately accounted rather than hidden by excluded match builtin.
